Must the palindrome condition consider the entire concatenated string of edge labels, or are single‑character strings automatically palindromes regardless of direction?
When multiple shortest palindrome paths exist, does the output require any specific tie‑breaking rule, or is any shortest length sufficient?
Is the length of a path defined as the number of edges traversed, the number of vertices visited, or the total number of characters in the concatenated label string?
Can the same edge be used multiple times within a single path, or must paths be simple (no repeated edges or vertices)?
Are there any constraints on the total length of a palindrome path (e.g., must it be ≤ N or can it be arbitrarily long), and how should potential infinite loops be handled?
Should the output values be separated by single spaces with no trailing spaces on each line, and must each line end with a newline character?

inline_prompts: We have a directed graph with N vertices, numbered 1, 2, \ldots, N. Information about the edges is given by N^2 characters C_{1, 1}, C_{1, 2}, \ldots, C_{1, N}, C_{2, 1}, \ldots, C_{N, N}. Here, each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -. If C_{i, j} is a lowercase English letter, then there is exactly one directed edge from vertex i to vertex j labeled C_{i, j}. If C_{i, j} is -, there is no edge from vertex i to vertex j. For each integer pair (i, j) with 1 \leq i, j \leq N, answer the following question: Among all paths from vertex i to vertex j whose concatenation of labels on the edges forms a palindrome, what is the length of the shortest such path? If there is no such path, the answer is -1. Note that a path of length zero (i.e., staying at vertex i when i = j) is considered a valid path with an empty string as its label. Print them in the following format: A_{1, 1} A_{1, 2} \ldots A_{1, N} A_{2, 1} A_{2, 2} \ldots A_{2, N} \vdots A_{N, 1} A_{N, 2} \ldots A_{N, N} Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 100 - N is an integer. - Each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -.
